newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas on waiting list, DAX stays unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Adidas on waiting list, DAX stays unchanged.

text.p: Sportswear maker Adidas AG will be allowed to join the DAX-30 index of blue-chips if two DAX firms merge before end September, German bourse operator Deutsche Boerse AG said late on Tuesday.
This leaves the DAX index of 30 German blue-chip shares unchanged -- for the time being at least.
There had been speculation that the German retailer Karstadt AG would be relegated from the DAX-30 index onto the MDAX index of German medium-sized firms, with its place taken by Adidas.

However, the planned mega-merger between the two German banks Bayerische Vereinsbank and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechselbank will leave a place free in the DAX-30 index if the merger is approved by Germany's cartel watchdog.
Analysts had said that this could help Karstadt avoid relegation and Adidas now looks set to take the place of one of the two Bavarian banks when they merge early next year.

Adidas has declined comment on the process of the bourse's annual review, which can sometimes be a political decision as banks on the panel push their favourite candidates, even ones in which they own shares.
Inclusion in the DAX index tends to stimulate demand for a stock as institutional investors reshuffle their portfolios to reflect the overall index.

But the top criteria had supported Adidas joining the DAX, as a key requirement is the so-called 35-35 rule, which says a DAX member must be among the top 35 in Germany in terms of both sales and capitalisation, according to industry analysts.
Recent German stock exchange data show Adidas occupying 27th position among German companies in terms of market capitalisation and 29th place in terms of sales.
Karstadt, on the other hand, held the 34th place in sales and was 44th in capitalisation. However, the merger between Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank seems to have allowed Karstadt a reprieve.

Deutsche Boerse confirmed that electronics and transport group Vossloh AG and recently-floated German savings, financing and insurance company BHW AG would be joining the MDAX index of 70 medium-sized firms in September.
Vossloh and BHW will replace German construction firm Strabag AG and insurer Volksfuersorge, which are relegated from the MDAX.
Volksfuersorge will leave the MDAX because another MDAX member, AMB Aachener und Muenchener Beteiligungen, owns more than 75 percent of Volksfuersorge.
Strabag is leaving the MDAX because it no longer belongs to the top 110 biggest public companies in terms of market capitalisation and turnover, the bourse said.
The companies will change places after September 19, so they will be officially introduced from September 22.
The decisions were made at a meeting of the German bourse operating company Deutsche Boerse.
